Aapoph Sovereign Guard.name: Aapoph Sovereign Guard
Aapoph Sovereign Guard.publicNotes:
Physically, aapoph sovereign guards tower over other aapophs, but their hulking stature and unquestioning obedience belie an intelligence unique even among the zyss. Despite their cunning, sovereign guards are rarely treacherous or self-serving; rather, each guard is expected to devote their existence solely to the advancement of their superiors. Even when beset on all sides by treacherous political machinations, zyss monarchs implicitly trust their sovereign guards, whose powerful bulk, keen senses, and whirling halberds are more dependable than any shield.

Serpentfolk society is riddled with secret organizations, many of which preserve long-lost traditions from the height of the ancient sekmin empire. Exclusive orders of aapoph sovereign guards and zyss assassins, among others, trace their origins back millennia, training in the same techniques they employed in the days when mammalian humanoids were nothing but servants or prey.

Aapoph Training

The towering aapophs employed as sovereign guards aren't born larger than their siblings. Rather, zyss trainers select certain aapoph hatchlings to be raised as guards. These young aapophs are reared in isolated nurseries where they're trained in advanced weaponcraft. According to rumor, the secret of a sovereign guard's increased cunning and stature lies in a diet regarded as blasphemous even by other sekmins.

Ayindilar Occultist.name: Ayindilar Occultist
Ayindilar Occultist.publicNotes:
Secretive groups of ayindilar occultists gather to worship otherworldly entities or pursue magics forbidden by their communities at large. Imbuing their weapons with mind-numbing psychic energy and utilizing their occult talents to confuse and confound foes, ayindilar occultists are the root of many of the biases outsiders feel toward their people.

In the days following Earthfall, many elves retreated from Golarion's surface to the gloom of the Darklands, founding city-states throughout the subterranean continents. Over generations, more and more of these sub-surface elves were born with physical colorations that matched the muted hues of their new home, with pale lavender skin and stark white hair eventually becoming the most common ayindilar complexion.

Today, little remains of the ancient ayindilar civilizations. Their great cities lie abandoned, and the underground trade routes they once traveled are now monster-infested tunnels. Ayindilar elves can be encountered throughout the Darklands, but they rarely gather in great numbers or seek attention. Most ayindilars are nomadic, avoiding contact with outsiders as they hunt prey or follow herds of moss-grazing lizards through lightless caverns. Others live in enclaves within larger cities, primarily on Nar-Voth, dwelling in the proverbial shadows cast by more established Darklands societies.

While some elven cultures embrace arcane, divine, or primal traditions, ayindilars are more interested in occult research, and many have learned to channel the psychic energies that permeate the Darklands. The magic practiced by ayindilars tends to be subtle, and their ability to cloud minds and remain hidden from sight has garnered them a reputation as sneaks and tricksters—a notoriety that fuels many ayindilars' own distrust of outsiders. Ironically, this mutual distrust drives some ayindilars to prey on surface folk and Darklands dwellers alike, further solidifying their sinister reputations.

Lost Cities

During their exodus from Golarion's surface, some ayindilar elves traveled through the Darklands all the way to Tian Xia, while others delved deeper toward the vaults of Orv. Most settled on Sekamina, building massive cities throughout. Their greatest city was Zirnakaynin, which legend holds was the birthplace of ayindilar occultism. For reasons unknown, Zirnakaynin fell. The other ayindilar city-states soon followed, and while many of these ruins have been reclaimed by other Darklands societies, lost Zirnakaynin remains mysterious and abandoned.

Cruelty of the Crowd

Today, ayindilar elves avoid congregating in large settlements, distrusting their own leaders nearly as much as they do outsiders. According to ayindilar lore, when more than a few thousand ayindilars gather in one place, their society undergoes sinister changes. Wicked behavior increasingly becomes the norm, as customs and institutions begin to echo those of the crueler ayindilar city-states. It's unclear whether this supposed phenomenon prompted ayindilars to abandon their ancient cities, but it certainly discourages modern ayindilar elves from returning to them.

action->Repair Ley Pylon.description:

The clockwork mage uses a mechanical wand as a focus to channel magical energy. This wand is built into the clockwork mage's chest, with only the crystal at the end exposed. Collapsing Vestibule.name: Collapsing Vestibule
Collapsing Vestibule.description: A weak point in the barrier between the Universe and the Plane of Earth compromises the stability of the entire chamber.

Collapsing Vestibule.routine: (2 actions) The hazard uses each of its actions to summon an elite @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.pathfinder-monster-core.Actor.ToteDLIM7jCyHwDH]{Stone Mauler}. Once the hazard has summoned a total of three stone maulers, it can’t summon another until the hazard resets. A reassembled stone mauler appears in the space it was destroyed with 100 Hit Points and is stunned 1. Corundumite.name: Corundumite
Corundumite.publicNotes:
Corundumites are flying earth elementals that look like faceted red or blue gemstones. Drawn to veins rich with rubies, sapphires, and other precious stones, corundumites regard themselves as the guardians of the earth's riches, attacking those who mine or even examine the uncut gems in their domains. They can be hostile to travelers who have gemstones in their possession, but those who carry no such stones—or who surrender their gems as recompense for the slight—are usually allowed to pass unharmed. Why corundumites are so protective of the stones in their care remains unknown, though those who have spoken with the elementals report that they seem to regard the gems not as symbols of wealth, but rather as living, thinking beings.

Gem Body

When it dies, a corundumite transforms into an inert—and highly valuable—corundum gemstone such as a ruby or sapphire. An intact gemstone harvested from a dead corundumite can be worth as much as 2,000 gp, provided it's in good condition. Unfortunately, not every battle leaves behind a perfectly preserved gemstone. If the damage that reduced the corundumite to 0 Hit Points was bludgeoning, force, or sonic damage, the gem smashes into 2d6 fragments, each of which is worth only 100 gp.

action->Gemsense.name: Gemsense
action->Gemsense.description: A corundumite can sense gems within 60 feet as if using the scent ability.

action->Glow.name: Glow
action->Glow.description: 20 feet. The aura sheds dim light.

action->Cold Ray.name: Cold Ray
action->Cold Ray.description:
The corundumite fires a beam of freezing blue light in a @Template[type:line|distance:60]. Any creature in the area takes @Damage[6d10[cold]|options:area-damage] damage and must attempt a @Check[reflex|dc:38|options:area-effect,damaging-effect,inflicts:immobilized,inflicts:petrified] save. The corundumite can't use Cold Ray on its next turn.

Critical Success No effect.

Success Half damage.

Failure Full damage and @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.eIcWbB5o3pP6OIMe]{Immobilized} for 1 round.

Critical Failure Full damage and @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.dTwPJuKgBQCMxixg]{Petrified} for 1 round. While petrified, the creature is transformed into solid ice instead of stone and gains weakness 5 to fire.

action->Earth Glide.name: Earth Glide
action->Earth Glide.description: The corundumite can Burrow through any earthen matter, including rock. When it does so, the corundumite moves at its full burrow Speed, leaving no tunnels or signs of its passing.

action->Fire Ray.name: Fire Ray
action->Fire Ray.description:
The corundumite fires a beam of blinding red light in a @Template[type:line|distance:60]. Any creature in the area takes deals @Damage[8d10[fire]|options:area-damage] damage and must attempt a @Check[reflex|dc:38|options:area-effect,damaging-effect,inflicts:dazzled,inflicts:blinded] DC save. Critical Success No effect.

Success Half damage.

Failure Full damage and @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.TkIyaNPgTZFBCCuh]{Dazzled} for 1 round.

Critical Failure Full damage and @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.XgEqL1kFApUbl5Z2]{Blinded} for 1 round.

action->Raking Shot.name: Raking Shot
action->Raking Shot.description: The corundumite uses Cold Ray or Fire Ray and then Flies in a straight line in a direction perpendicular to its ray. During this movement, the ray moves with the corundumite. When the ray enters a creature's space, that creature is affected by the ray. The corundumite can't use Raking Shot again for [[/gmr 1d4 #Recharge Raking Shot]]{1d4 rounds}.

Crushing Threshold.name: Crushing Threshold
Crushing Threshold.description: The ceilings of four alcoves slam down, threatening to crush everything inside.
Crushing Threshold.disable: @Check[thievery|dc:40] (master) twice to @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.actionspf2e.Item.2EE4aF4SZpYf0R6H]{Pick the Lock} of the iron door or @Check[athletics|dc:44] (master) to [[/act force-open]] the door
Crushing Threshold.reset: Once the ceiling of the northernmost alcove descends, all four ceilings return to their original positions, the wall of force sealing the northern alcove disappears, and the hazard resets. Opening the iron door (even from the opposite side) permanently disables the hazard.
Crushing Threshold.routine: (1 action) The ceiling of one of the four alcoves—starting with the southernmost alcove and moving one alcove north each round—slams down with incredible force. A creature bracing the ceiling can prevent it from descending by making a successful @Check[athletics|dc:44] check, but the creature must repeat this check each round. The ceiling drops if the creature fails the check or leaves the alcove. Creatures and objects in an alcove when a ceiling drops each take @Damage[(6d12+41)[bludgeoning]|options:area-damage] damage (@Check[fortitude|dc:44|basic|options:area-effect|options:inflicts:prone] save). A creature that takes this damage also falls @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.j91X7x0XSomq8d60]{Prone}. The contents of the alcove are then teleported to the secret hallway north of area H2, leaving the alcove filled with nothing but a block of solid stone.

action->Welcome to the Coils.description:

Effect Zyphaniss's telepathic chuckle echoes in the minds of all creatures in the area. action->Twin Bond.description: Daehalyan can communicate telepathically with Kajasiel as long as they are within 100 feet of each other.

action->Sovereign Aura.name: Sovereign Aura
action->Sovereign Aura.description: 15 feet. Daehalyan's presence bolsters his followers. Allies in his aura gain a +2 status bonus to attack rolls, AC, and saving throws, and at the start of their turn gain 10 temporary Hit Points that last until the start of their next turn.

action->Spare Sibling.name: Spare Sibling
action->Spare Sibling.description: Daehalyan's bond with Kajasiel is such that he can avoid magically harming his twin. If his next action is to Cast a Spell that doesn't have a duration and Kajasiel would be in the spell's area, the spell doesn't target Kajasiel.

action->Gestalt.name: Gestalt
action->Gestalt.description: Death grants the following additional spells to any gestalt he joins: @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.spells-srd.Item.ZMvplR106Jxl7B15]{Awaken Entropy}, @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.spells-srd.Item.8THDHP0UC7SgOYYF]{Inevitable Disaster}.

Effect If the target gets a success or critical success on the triggering save, it instead gets an outcome one degree of success worse than the result of the roll.

armor->Leather Apron.name: Leather Apron
armor->Leather Apron.description: A mix of flexible and molded boiled leather, a suit of this type of armor provides some protection with maximum flexibility.

action->Grave Weapon.name: Grave Weapon
action->Grave Weapon.description: The wight is bound to a dagger it was buried with. Other wights can be bound to different weapons.

action->Fueled by Spite.name: Fueled by Spite
action->Fueled by Spite.description: Each time a creature loses Hit Points due to a corrupting spite curse the wight inflicted, the wight gains 3 temporary Hit Points.

action->Corrupting Spite.name: Corrupting Spite

The wight's unarmed attacks and bound weapons inflict a curse that makes a creature grow weak and spiteful. If a wight inflicts corrupting spite on a creature already afflicted by it, the victim attempts a new save, ignoring the result if it's better than a failure.

action->Three-Headed.name: Three-Headed

Losing a head doesn't kill a chimera (as long as it has at least one head left), but it does prevent it from making Strikes with the lost head or using any abilities granted by the head.

action->Fire Breath.name: Fire Breath
action->Fire Breath.description: Doomcrier's magma worm head exhales a blast of flame in a @Template[type:cone|distance:30] that deals @Damage[16d6[fire]|options:area-damage] damage to all creatures in the area (@Check[reflex|dc:36|basic|options:area-effect] save). It can't use Fire Breath again for [[/gmr 1d4 #Recharge Fire Breath]]{1d4 rounds}.

action->Multiple Reactions.name: Multiple Reactions
action->Multiple Reactions.description: A greater chimera gains 2 extra reactions each round that it can use only to make Reactive Strikes. It must use a different head for each reaction, and it can't use more than one on the same triggering action. If it loses one of its heads, it also loses one of these extra reactions.

action->Storm Blast.name: Storm Blast
action->Storm Blast.description: Doomcrier's thunderbird head blasts its foes with peals of thunder and crackling bolts of lightning. Each creature in a @Template[type:emanation|distance:30] takes @Damage[8d6[electricity],8d6[sonic]|options:area-damage] damage (@Check[reflex|dc:36|basic] save). Doomcrier can't use Lightning Blast for [[/gmr 1d4 #rounds]]{1d4 rounds}.

action->Three-Headed Strike.name: Three-Headed Strike
action->Three-Headed Strike.description: The greater chimera makes a Strike with each of its heads, each at a –2 penalty and targeting a different creature. These Strikes count as only one attack for the greater chimera's multiple attack penalty, and the penalty doesn't increase until after it has made all three attacks.

action->Vision of Doom.name: Vision of Doom
action->Vision of Doom.description:
A creature hit by Doomcrier's black dog jaws Strike sees visions of their own doom. The creature must attempt a @Check[will|dc:36|options:inflicts:doomed,inflicts:frightened] save. If Doomcrier critically hits, the creature also becomes @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.3uh1r86TzbQvosxv]{Doomed 1} for as long as they are frightened by vision of doom.

Critical Success The creature is unaffected and immune to vision of doom for 24 hours.

Success The creature is @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.TBSHQspnbcqxsmjL]{Frightened 1}.

Failure The creature is @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.TBSHQspnbcqxsmjL]{Frightened 2}.

Critical Failure The creature is @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.TBSHQspnbcqxsmjL]{Frightened 4}.

Dragonfire Fly.name: Dragonfire Fly
Dragonfire Fly.publicNotes:
A dragonfire fly is an immense dragonfly with wings veined in delicate traceries of red fire. Its faceted eyes are huge gemstones that blaze with internal luminescence. While on the hunt, the dragonfire fly zips through subterranean labyrinths or clings silently to cavern walls, lancing prey with solid jets of flame cast from its eyes.

Although dragonfire flies most often use fire to catch their food, they adapt readily to their enemies' weapons and defenses. When magic harms a dragonfire fly, the fly's eyes and the flames across its wings change color, burning with white frost, yellow electricity, or whatever other energy it was exposed to. This same energy burns in the dragonfire fly's eye rays.

Opal Eyes

If a dragonfire fly’s eyes resemble gems, it’s because they are! Both of a dragonfire fly’s multifaceted eyes are immense, translucent opals as large as a human head. The gems change hue when the fly’s flame takes on a new color, and they retain this color when the dragonfire fly dies. Each of the fly’s eyes is worth at least 10,000 gold—if a buyer for such a large single stone can be found.

action->Barrel Roll.name: Barrel Roll
action->Barrel Roll.description:
Trigger While Flying, the dragonfire fly is hit by a ranged Strike that deals physical damage

Effect The fly spins in flight, deflecting some of the force of the attack. The fly gains resistance 15 to physical damage from the triggering attack.

action->Fire Wings.name: Fire Wings
action->Fire Wings.description:
When the fly is first encountered, the fly's wings burn with red flame. When the fly takes acid, cold, electricity, fire, sonic, or void damage, the fly's wing flame color changes depending on the type of damage dealt. If an attack or effect deals more than one of these damage types, the fly chooses which damage type affects their fire wings color. The fly gains resistance 15 to the damage type associated with its new fire wings color, and its eye beam ranged Strike deals that damage type. After 1 minute, the fly's fire wings revert to red flame. The damage type, fire color, and other effects of each fire wings color are:

Acid: Green fire. A creature that starts their turn in the fly's firelight aura takes @Damage[3d6[persistent,acid]] damage.

Cold: White fire. A creature that starts their turn in the fly's firelight aura takes a –15-foot status penalty to its Speeds for 1 round.

Electricity: Yellow fire. A creature that starts their turn in the fly's firelight aura is @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.i3OJZU2nk64Df3xm]{Clumsy 1} for 1 round.

Fire: Red fire. A creature that starts their turn in the fly's firelight aura takes @Damage[6d6[fire]] damage with a @Check[reflex|dc:32|basic] save.

Sonic: Purple fire. The fly emits a loud buzz. A creature is @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.9PR9y0bi4JPKnHPR]{Deafened} while in the fly's firelight aura.

Void: Black fire. The fly becomes @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.DmAIPqOBomZ7H95W]{Concealed} and loses its firelight aura until its Fire Wings change to a different color.

action->Firelight.name: Firelight
action->Firelight.description: 30 feet. The aura sheds dim light of the same color as the fly's current fire wings color.

action->Carry.name: Carry
action->Carry.description: The fly can Fly at half Speed while it has a creature @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.kWc1fhmv9LBiTuei]{Grabbed} or @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.VcDeM8A5oI6VqhbM]{Restrained} in its mandibles, carrying that creature along with it.

Dream Cradle of the Dark Tapestry.name: Dream Cradle of the Dark Tapestry
Dream Cradle of the Dark Tapestry.description: Long ago, Yig revealed that some of his sekmin children slept deep beneath the Kodar Mountains. In response, his surface-dwelling worshippers developed this item to navigate the Darklands' vast chasms in search of the Great Old One's lost progeny. When the dream cradle of the Dark Tapestry is activated as a single action with the concentrate trait, over the course of 1 minute, the fist-sized egg expands to the size of a hot-air balloon, to which a basket or other platform can be attached.
Dream Cradle of the Dark Tapestry.pilotingCheck: Arcana (DC 30), Religion (DC 32), Occultism (DC 30), or Piloting Lore (DC 29)

action->Burst.name: Burst
action->Burst.description: When the dream cradle is destroyed, the egg-balloon shatters, releasing a cloud of nightmarish oneiric energy. Creatures other than the pilot and passengers within 30 feet of the dream cradle take @Damage[14d6[mental]|options:area-damage] damage (@Check[will|dc:32|basic|options:area-effect,inflicts:fleeing,inflicts:frightened] save). On a failed save, the creature is also @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.TBSHQspnbcqxsmjL]{Frightened 2} (@UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.TBSHQspnbcqxsmjL]{Frightened 4} and @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.sDPxOjQ9kx2RZE8D]{Fleeing} for 1 round on a critical failure). The dream cradle then uses that last of its magical reserves to cast @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.spells-srd.Item.A2JfEKe6BZcTG1S8]{Fly} on the pilot and each passenger.

action->Recharge.name: Recharge
action->Recharge.description: Each day, the dream cradle can be used for up to 1 hour before it shrinks back into its egg form to recharge for 8 hours. One minute before it shrinks, the balloon wobbles in warning, giving the pilot time to land.

action->Vertical Travel.name: Vertical Travel
action->Vertical Travel.description: The dream cradle's Speed doubles while moving straight up or down

spell->Truesight (Constant).name:
<Compendium> tag will get replaced with text from compendium entry @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.spells-srd.Item.uqlxMQQeSGWEVjki]
Truesight (Constant)

spell->Truespeech (Constant).name:
<Compendium> tag will get replaced with text from compendium entry @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.spells-srd.Item.SwUiVavHKMWG7t5K]
Truespeech (Constant)

action->Rejuvenation.name: Rejuvenation
action->Rejuvenation.description: Phreygia's echo persists until Yig wills her out of existence. Even if destroyed, she returns within [[/gmr 1d4 #days]]{1d4 days}, restored completely with full Hit Points and no conditions.

action->Coiling Essence.name: Coiling Essence
action->Coiling Essence.description: Phreygia's spirit briefly takes the form of an enormous serpent. Phreygia Flies twice. All creatures in her path attempt a @Check[reflex|dc:37|options:area-effect,inflicts:immobilized] save. On a failure, the creature is @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.eIcWbB5o3pP6OIMe]{Immobilized} by ectoplasm. Each round a creature ends its turn still stuck in ectoplasm, it takes @Damage[8d6[void]] damage (@Check[fortitude|dc:37|basic] save).

Eroded Vault Lifter.name: Eroded Vault Lifter
Eroded Vault Lifter.publicNotes:
Vault lifters are sentient stone constructs roughly carved into the semblance of giant xiomorns. Each vault lifter is encircled by a spinning ring, called a rotor, which grants the lifter the ability to fly.

Xiomorns created vault lifters to help construct their vaults throughout the Plane of Earth and across the Universe. With the ability to airlift heavy burdens and possessed with enough intelligence to carry out complex instructions, vault lifters were valuable lieutenants in the xiomorns' vast terraforming projects. Vault lifters were intended to be more than simple laborers, however; they were also built as weapons of war. In combat, vault lifters spin their rotors into fearsome buzz saws capable of propelling them at high speeds and slicing foes in half.

Abandoned Guardians

While some vault lifters continue to serve living xiomorns, others have been left behind in long-abandoned locations. Over the years, many of these forgotten vault lifters have completed their assignments and deactivated themselves. Others continue to perform some unending task, such as "keep this area clean," "prevent unauthorized entry," or "I'll be back in a bit—wait for my return." After millennia spent in solitude, some abandoned vault lifters become fanatical about their final orders, spinning them into complex philosophical systems heavy with moral significance.

action->Overgrown.name: Overgrown
action->Overgrown.description: These vault lifters have been partially reclaimed by the elements. At the start of an encounter, the lifter is @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.xYTAsEpcJE1Ccni3]{Slowed 2} until the end of its first turn.

action->Activate Rotor.name: Activate Rotor
action->Activate Rotor.description:
The vault lifter's rotor spins, becoming a buzzing blur. While the rotor is activated, the lifter gains a fly Speed of 40 feet. The spinning rotor also creates an aura in a @Template[type:emanation|distance:5] around the lifter. Any creature that enters or starts its turn in the area must attempt a @Check[fortitude|dc:34|options:damaging-effect,forced-movement,inflicts:prone] save.

Critical Success The creature is unaffected, and the vault lifter's rotor is deactivated. The lifter loses its fly Speed and aura until it Activates Rotor again.

Success The creature takes @Damage[2d8[slashing]|options:area-damage] damage.

Failure The creature takes @Damage[4d8[slashing]|options:area-damage] damage.

Critical Failure The creature takes @Damage[8d8[slashing]|options:area-damage] damage. If the creature isn't @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.kWc1fhmv9LBiTuei]{Grabbed} or @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.VcDeM8A5oI6VqhbM]{Restrained} by the vault lifter, they are pushed back 15 feet and knocked @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.j91X7x0XSomq8d60]{Prone}.

action->Carry.name: Carry
action->Carry.description: A vault lifter can Fly at half Speed while it has a creature @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.kWc1fhmv9LBiTuei]{Grabbed} or @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.VcDeM8A5oI6VqhbM]{Restrained}, carrying that creature along with it.

action->Draw In.name: Draw In
action->Draw In.description: The vault lifter attempts to [[/act reposition]] a creature it has @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.kWc1fhmv9LBiTuei]{Grabbed} or @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.VcDeM8A5oI6VqhbM]{Restrained}, moving the creature into a space adjacent to it. This attempt neither applies nor counts toward the lifter's multiple attack penalty.

action->Overdrive.name: Overdrive
action->Overdrive.description:
Requirements The vault lifter's rotor is activated

Effect The lifter Flies up to three times its Fly Speed in a straight line without triggering reactions. At the end of this flight, the lifter must attempt a @Check[fortitude|dc:40] saving throw. On a failure, the lifter's rotor is deactivated.

Etumult.name: Etumult
Etumult.publicNotes:
In ancient times, a cabal of primalists imbued an amalgam of beasts with both supernatural might and a hatred of magic itself, hoping to achieve a potent weapon for use against arcane spellcasters. Effective beyond expectation, the first leydroths broke free and turned on their creators. Worse, the leydroths bred true, and these reclusive predators have long outlived their original creators.

Leydroths look like distorted, apelike felines with many-branching horns growing from the backs of their heads. Their thickly muscled limbs end in glowing claws.
Etumult.saveDetails: +2 status to all saves vs. magic

spell->Dispel Magic (At Will).name:
<Compendium> tag will get replaced with text from compendium entry @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.spells-srd.Item.9HpwDN4MYQJnW0LG]
Dispel Magic (At Will)

action->Magic Sense.name: Magic Sense
action->Magic Sense.description: The leydroth detects the source and school of each source of magic within 60 feet as an imprecise sense.

action->+2 Status to All Saves vs. Magic.name: +2 Status to All Saves vs. Magic

action->Menace to Magic.name: Menace to Magic
action->Menace to Magic.description:
Trigger A creature within 60 feet Casts a Spell

Effect The leydroth attempts an @Check[intimidation] check to counteract the triggering spell.

action->Dispelling Roar.name: Dispelling Roar
action->Dispelling Roar.description:
The leydroth unleashes a bestial roar that reverberates within a @Template[emanation|distance:30]. It rolls an Intimidation check and compares the result to the Will DC of each creature in the area, with the effects of @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.actionspf2e.Item.2u915NdUyQan6uKF]{Demoralize}.

It also uses this result to attempt to counteract each spell or magical effect in the area, plus one item or effect on each creature in the area, with the effects of @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.spells-srd.Item.9HpwDN4MYQJnW0LG]{Dispel Magic}.

The leydroth can't use Dispelling Roar again for [[/gmr 1d4 #Recharge Dispelling Roar]]{1d4 rounds}.

action->Dispelling Strike.name: Dispelling Strike
action->Dispelling Strike.description:
Frequency once per round

Trigger The leydroth hits a creature, object, or spell effect with a Strike

Effect The leydroth casts its innate @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.spells-srd.Item.9HpwDN4MYQJnW0LG]{Dispel Magic}, targeting one effect on the creature struck.

action->Spell Feedback.name: Spell Feedback
action->Spell Feedback.description: Any time a leydroth counteracts a spell or item, the spell's caster or the creature holding the item takes @Damage[8d6[mental]] damage (@Check[will|dc:38|basic] save).

Facetal Branch.name: Facetal Branch
Facetal Branch.publicNotes:
Facetal branches are elder facetals whose gemstone bodies have grown into large glowing crystals. Instead of donning humanoid guises as facetal nodes do, facetal branches use hardlight to project insect-like bodies in the image of their deity, Sairazul.

With minds capable of revisiting their memories with crystalline perfection, facetal branches can both move and communicate across space and time. They're named after the constant improvements they make to their past selves, navigating branches of alternate histories to achieve crystalline perfection.

Gathering Moss

While their younger cousins, facetal nodes, travel to accumulate knowledge, facetal branches turn their explorations inwards, scrutinizing past actions for minor imperfections that could stunt their slow, crystalline growth. When they identify a flaw, they can reach backwards in time to alter their past—but only if their past self occupies the same location as their present one. For this reason, facetal branches tend to stay put.

action->Temporal Telepathy.name: Temporal Telepathy
action->Temporal Telepathy.description: The facetal branch can communicate telepathically with themselves at a specific moment in the past, provided their past self occupies the branch's current space.

action->Gem Form.name: Gem Form
action->Gem Form.description:
When a facetal node is reduced to 0 Hit Points, their hardlight body is destroyed, leaving behind the node's true form, a Tiny glowing gemstone. In this form, the node's Speed is 0, they're immune to damage, and they're deactivated. While deactivated, they can't take actions or speak, although they can use telepathy. The node remains deactivated until it reactivates at a time determined by the GM (usually after decades or more).

While deactivated, the facetal branch can't use temporal telepathy, and their luminescent aura is deactivated.

action->Luminescent Aura.name: Luminescent Aura
action->Luminescent Aura.description: 30 feet. The facetal branch's glowing gem fills the area of the aura with bright light. The branch can deactivate or activate its aura as a single action with the concentrate trait.

action->Blinding Attack.name: Blinding Attack
action->Blinding Attack.description: On a critical hit with a gem ray Strike, the target is @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.XgEqL1kFApUbl5Z2]{Blinded} for 1 round.

action->Blinking Strobe.name: Blinking Strobe
action->Blinking Strobe.description:
The node's gem coruscates with light. Enemies within a @Template[type:emanation|distance:30] must attempt a @Check[fortitude|dc:40|options:area-effect,inflicts:dazzled,inflicts:blinded] save.

Critical Success The creature is unaffected.

Success The creature is @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.TkIyaNPgTZFBCCuh]{Dazzled} for 1 round.

Failure The creature is @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.XgEqL1kFApUbl5Z2]{Blinded} for 1 round.

Critical Failure As failure, and the target is teleported to a space of the node's choice within 30 feet that the node can see.

action->Hardlight Projection.name: Hardlight Projection
action->Hardlight Projection.description: The node projects a new Huge, insect-like form around itself, changing its appearance but not its statistics. The node's projected form is a solid body made of hardlight. While using a projected form, the node's true form, a Tiny gem, is always visible embedded in the projection's abdomen or thorax. The gemstone is the facetal's sensory organ, and if the gemstone is covered, the facetal node is @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.XgEqL1kFApUbl5Z2]{Blinded}.

action->Temporal Skip.name: Temporal Skip
action->Temporal Skip.description:
The facetal branch can pluck creatures from the very flow of time. One creature the branch can see within 30 feet must attempt a @Check[fortitude|dc:40] save. The branch can target themself, automatically failing their save.

Critical Success The creature is unaffected and becomes temporarily immune to Temporal Skip for 24 hours.

Success The creature is @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.dfCMdR4wnpbYNTix]{Stunned 1}.

Failure The creature winks out of existence for 1 round (or for up to 1 hour if the branch targeted themself). Until the creature reappears, time doesn't pass for the creature. When the effect ends, the creature returns to the space it occupied when it disappeared or to the nearest space if the original is now filled.

Facetal Node.name: Facetal Node
Facetal Node.publicNotes:
Facetal nodes are the youngest facetals, having lived for mere tens of thousands of years. Though nearly eternal from the viewpoint of mortals, nodes measure their lives on a geological time scale, regarding themselves as neophytes compared to elder facetals and other immortal elementals. Most facetal nodes travel far and wide to gather knowledge, using their projected humanoid bodies to blend in among other sentient beings. They tend to observe the affairs of mortals impassively, unmoved by hardships which, from their perspective, last no longer than the blink of an eye.

Formed under immense geological pressure over untold eons, facetals are intelligent, eloquent elemental gemstones. While facetals can’t affect the world in their true gem forms, they can focus their inner radiance to create corporeal bodies made of hardlight.

Everpresent Gem

No matter what form they project to the world, a facetal node's true body—their gem—is always visible somewhere on their hardlight body. Since a facetal node senses the world through this gemstone, they often go to great pains to hide the stone's significance, disguising it as an ordinary piece of jewelry, the crystal on the tip of a walking staff, or some other mundane jewel. A facetal's gem is functionally unbreakable, requiring the will of a god or similar force to shatter it.

action->Gem Form.name: Gem Form
action->Gem Form.description: When a facetal node is reduced to 0 Hit Points, their hardlight body is destroyed, leaving behind the node's true form, a Tiny glowing gemstone. In this form, the node's Speed is 0, they're immune to damage, and they're deactivated. While deactivated, they can't take actions or speak, although they can use telepathy. The node remains deactivated until it reactivates at a time determined by the GM (usually after decades or more).

action->Blinding Attack.name: Blinding Attack
action->Blinding Attack.description: On a critical hit with a gem ray Strike, the target is @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.XgEqL1kFApUbl5Z2]{Blinded} for 1 round.

action->Blinking Strobe.name: Blinking Strobe
action->Blinking Strobe.description:
The node's gem coruscates with light. Enemies within a @Template[type:emanation|distance:30] must attempt a @Check[fortitude|dc:37|options:area-effect,inflicts:dazzled,inflicts:blinded] save.

Critical Success The creature is unaffected.

Success The creature is @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.TkIyaNPgTZFBCCuh]{Dazzled} for 1 round.

Failure The creature is @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.XgEqL1kFApUbl5Z2]{Blinded} for 1 round.

Critical Failure As failure, and the target is teleported to a space of the node's choice within 30 feet that the node can see.

action->Hardlight Projection.name: Hardlight Projection
action->Hardlight Projection.description: The node projects a new Small or Medium humanoid form around itself, changing its appearance but not its statistics. The node's projected form is a solid body made of hardlight. While using a projected form, the node's true form, a Tiny gem, is always visible somewhere on the projection, such as set into a piece of jewelry. The gemstone is the facetal's sensory organ, and if the gemstone is covered, the facetal node is @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.XgEqL1kFApUbl5Z2]{Blinded}.

False Prayer.name: False Prayer
False Prayer.description: A statue dedicated to Ydersius fills the chamber with the divine glory of the Father of Serpents.
False Prayer.disable: @Check[deception|dc:43] (master) to falsely proclaim the party's devotion to Ydersius, @Check[religion|dc:41] (master) to rededicate the statue to Yig, or @Check[thievery|dc:38] (expert) twice to pry the statue's eyes from their sockets
False Prayer.reset: Unless the statue is destroyed, both its eyes are removed, or the statue is rededicated to Yig, the hazard deactivates and resets 1 minute after no living creatures are in the room.
False Prayer.routine: (2 actions) The statue uses each of its two actions to cast a 9th-rank @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.spells-srd.Item.ZxHC7V7HtjUsB8zH]{Blazing Bolt} spell (DC 41), targeting up to three living creatures per casting. For each eye removed from the statue, the hazard has 1 fewer action. Until the beginning of the statue's next turn, the doors to area H17 don't require an Athletics check to @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.actionspf2e.Item.SjmKHgI7a5Z9JzBx]{Force Open} (but opening them still requires an Interact action).

action->Divine Command.name: Divine Command
action->Divine Command.description:
Trigger A creature moves adjacent to the doors to area H17 or attempts to disable the hazard and fails

Effect The light from the statue's eyes intensifies. The statue casts @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.spells-srd.Item.fkDeKktdmbeplYRY]{Overwhelming Presence} (@Check[will|dc:41|options:area-effect,item:type:spell|traits:auditory,concentrate,incapacitation,manipulate,mental,visual]), targeting each living creature in the room. The hazard then rolls initiative.

Fate of Eivess.name: Fate of Eivess
Fate of Eivess.description: The restless spirits of the prophet Eivess and his followers force intruders to relive their deaths at the fangs of Yig's avatar.
Fate of Eivess.disable: @Check[society|dc:38] (master) or @Check[religion|dc:40] (master) to convince the spirits that their horror has been over for millennia, or @Check[occultism|dc:38] (master) or @Check[intimidation|dc:42] to recognize that this avatar exists only in the memories of the tormented spirits and command it to stand down; three total successes are required to disable the haunt
Fate of Eivess.routine: (3 actions) The avatar uses its first action each round to Devour Faithful, then attempts to Strike and swallow a frightened creature within 20 feet. If no nearby creatures are frightened, the avatar continues using its actions to Devour Faithful until a frightened victim becomes available.

action->Massacre.name: Massacre
action->Massacre.description:
Trigger Eivess places the last of the eggs on the ground and calls for Yig to appear

Effect The towering serpent rises over the hill and snatches Eivess in its jaws, swallowing him whole and sparking mass panic among his followers, with the effects of Devour Faithful. The haunt rolls initiative.

action->Devour Faithful.name: Devour Faithful
action->Devour Faithful.description: The avatar of Yig seizes a nearby follower and gulps them down. The terrifying sight deals @Damage[(3d10+15)[mental]|options:area-damage] damage to all creatures within 30 feet (@Check[will|dc:30|basic|options:area-effect,inflicts:frightened] save). Any creature that takes this mental damage is @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.TBSHQspnbcqxsmjL]{Frightened 1}, or @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.TBSHQspnbcqxsmjL]{Frightened 2} on a critical failure.

action->Swallow Whole.name: Swallow Whole
action->Swallow Whole.description:
Huge, @Damage[(3d10+15)[mental]], Rupture 40

A swallowed creature hurtles through a terrifying vortex of indistinct shadows, surrounded by the distant wails of swallowed pilgrims. They can't reduce their @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.TBSHQspnbcqxsmjL]{Frightened} value below 1 until they [[/act escape]] or cut themselves free.

@Localize[PF2E.NPC.Abilities.Glossary.SwallowWhole]

Fleshwarp Fetters.name: Fleshwarp Fetters
Fleshwarp Fetters.description: A surge of fleshwarping magic twists creatures' limbs, especially those used to move.
Fleshwarp Fetters.disable: @Check[arcana|dc:30] (trained) or @Check[occultism|dc:30] (expert) to disrupt the magic, or @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.spells-srd.Item.9HpwDN4MYQJnW0LG]{Dispel Magic} (6th rank, DC 28) to counteract the fleshwarping

action->Hobble.name: Hobble
action->Hobble.description:
Trigger A creature enters the area marked T on the map

Effect Each creature in the marked area must attempt a @Check[fortitude|dc:32] save.

General Vesperix.name: General Vesperix
General Vesperix.publicNotes:
Xiomorn troopers are an elite military force formed from the ranks of xiomorn vault keepers. Armed with technology only they understand, xiomorn troopers hold the line against those who oppose the mysterious aims of the vault builders.

Many xiomorn troopers possess special training or equipment that helps them perform specific roles within their strike force. Comm troopers, for example, can communicate telepathically with their fellow troopers, while scout troopers surround themselves with fields of light-bending energy on their patrols. The batons of shock troopers carry charges of electricity that they use to stun their foes, while rad troopers are armed with explosives that release bursts of a sickening radiation, to which the troopers themselves are immune.

Mysterious Generals

Some xiomorn troopers consider themselves part of a single military organization led by a figure whose identity is unknown even to the highest-ranking troopers. Referred to only as the "Commander," this mysterious leader hands down orders along an extended, telepathic chain of command. In many Orvian vaults, the Commander is presumed to be a vault builder—or perhaps a fellow trooper in direct contact with the builders—though some troopers insist the Commander is simply an imaginary figurehead created to inspire loyalty. The fact that different squads of troopers have at times been given conflicting orders lends credence to the latter belief.

Knucklehead.name: Knucklehead
Knucklehead.publicNotes:
Knuckleheads are fleshwarps named after the oversized hand that sprouts from their neck in place of a skull. Their dangling, armor-plated arms are equally disproportionate, even in comparison to their massive frames, which range in size from 10 to 14 feet tall. Knuckleheads can use their arms either as a second pair of legs or to deliver stone-shattering punches. They feed by crushing a victim in their head-hand, the palm of which is split by a toothy maw.

It's often said that encountering a fleshwarp is evidence there's an even greater monster nearby: the cruel being that tortured the fleshwarp into its distorted form. The Darklands are home to many such monsters, both the fleshwarps and their creators.

Failed Experiments

Knuckleheads are the product of an effort to turn prisoners into obedient servants, but it turns out that a brain isn't an optional luxury when creating the perfect laborer. Driven by hunger and blind instinct, knuckleheads hunted their creators and fellow prisoners alike. Now that they've escaped into the Darklands, they prowl pitch-black caverns, attracted by the smell of flesh.

Monofilamental.name: Monofilamental
Monofilamental.publicNotes:
A monofilamental is a floating bubble made of glowing, crystalline strands. From this complex web of interconnected threads, a highly ordered intelligence emerges, one capable of turning each of its delicate skeins into an unbreakable, serrating lash.

Drifting through the Darklands on subterranean air currents, a monofilamental looks as delicate as a soap bubble or spider web. In fact, the psychic intelligence that animates the monofilamental exerts an unbreakable mental control over each of its strands, granting them unrivaled tensile strength. A single monofilamental thread can slice through steel or stone, to say nothing of the flesh and bone toward which the construct unerringly drifts. If monofilamental thread could be harvested, it would both be a powerful tool and a fearsome weapon; when a monofilamental dies, however, so too does the mental force that fortifies each thread.

Collective Network

Although intelligent, monofilamentals are spun by—and exist only to serve—a species of non-sapient spiders native to the Plane of Earth. Working collectively through instinct, clusters of these extraplanar spiders spin webs of unmatched complexity, some of which awaken to sentience as monofilamentals. Once created, a monofilamental bends its brilliant psychic intellect toward a narrow purpose: fetching meat for its arachnid creators.

A ravener who goes more than a week without successfully using Consume Soul to feed on a dying creature starves, and their soul ward loses @Damage[1d4[untyped]] Hit Points each day until they feed. Radlight Cap.name: Radlight Cap
Radlight Cap.publicNotes:
The radlights caps that flourish in many parts of Nar-Voth look like softly glowing, halfling-sized toadstools: a relatively common sight in the Darklands. When radlight caps change color, however, their dangerous nature becomes evident. With each color change, the fungi gain a new set of stimuli that trigger their deadly spore clouds. While a field of blue mushrooms may have attacked noisy interlopers, when they shift to red they assault anyone who moves a muscle. Many Nar-Voth natives, even non-sentient ones, have learned the colors and corresponding behaviors that will see them safely through a field of radlight caps.

Red Light, Green Light

Ayindilar elves claim that they originally cultivated radlight caps as an advanced warning system against radiation, and that the fungus's other color changes are merely an unintended mutation. Regardless, their original function remains useful enough that the elves rarely eradicate growths of radlight caps. Rather, they teach this warning rhyme to those who must pass through a radlight forest:

Red light stop,
Yellow drop.
Green light rush,
Blue light hush.
Black for terror, black for flight,
For this way comes the sickness light.

Multiple radlight caps encountered within 100 feet of each other synchronize their color changes, such that all caps are the same color at the same time.

At the start of each round, if a radlight cap is within 100 feet of an object or creature that emits radiation, the radlight cap's color changes to black. While black, the radlight cap loses its Radlight aura and can't take actions or reactions.

The type of damage dealt and an additional effect is determined by the radlight cap's current color.

  • Green The spores deal force damage. Creatures that fail their save are pushed 10 feet away from the radlight cap.

Shivver.name: Shivver
Shivver.publicNotes:
In some Darklands cultures, prisoners are routinely fleshwarped into grotesque shapes at the whims of their cruel captors. These unfortunate victims are dubbed "shivvers" after the thrill of horror they elicit and as a nod to one of the more infamous Darklands prisons. Once ordinary humanoids, shivvers now sport wriggling tentacles, insectile mandibles, and other bizarre "improvements." The agony these modifications cause is enough to drive many shivvers into murderous rages.

It's often said that encountering a fleshwarp is evidence there's an even greater monster nearby: the cruel being that tortured the fleshwarp into its distorted form. The Darklands are home to many such monsters, both the fleshwarps and their creators.

Fugitives of the Shiv

While some prisons pride themselves on being inescapable, the wardens of the Shiv once routinely released their more "artistically" fleshwarped captives before their sentences were fully served. The wardens believed that the products of their cruel punishments would inspire fear and obedience throughout the Darklands.

The greenish pall that sicklight wisps cast over their surroundings causes creatures within it to sicken and die. Whereas the will-o'-wisps typically encountered on the surface feed on fear, sicklight wisps feast on the illness they spread, taking joy in robbing creatures of their vigor and health.

Though most commonly associated with the pit of Mobhad Leigh, sicklight wisps are occasionally encountered elsewhere in the Darklands. Wicked creatures sometimes employ the wisps to foil attempts at scrying on their subterranean lairs, as anyone who uses magic to spy upon a sicklight wisp risks having their mind irrevocably shattered.

Curse of the Infirm

In the Darklands, sicklight wisps are feared by both healers and the sick, because they're drawn to hospitals and other places of healing. Able to travel invisibly and evade scrying, the wisps slip into sickrooms, becoming briefly visible as they drain the remaining life from ailing victims. To protect against the wisps, some long-standing institutions of healing have taken to planting radlight caps around their facilities, since these otherwise dangerous mushrooms turn black in the presence of even an invisible sicklight wisp.

Sorcerous Skull Swarm.publicNotes:
The act of creating a demilich sometimes goes horribly awry, leaving behind a shattered remnant of a once-mighty spellcaster constantly leaking eldritch energies. The ruined spirit animates a cloud of debased copies of itself, glittering with cracked crystals in crude imitation, and it hungers constantly for the magical energies denied it in its corrupted immortality.

Some of the spellcaster's personality remains in the swarm, albeit usually unnaturally split between the skulls. As a consequence, the skulls argue among themselves as warring parts of the personality clamor to be heard, resulting in the swarm's fractious, inconstant attitude.

A skull swarm is composed of reanimated masses of craniums and jawbones, forming a terrifying avalanche of undead fury. Most skull swarms are mindless, though some retain a vestige of wit, awareness, and even magical talents from life, culminating in a highly intelligent swarm mind.

Strangleroot.name: Strangleroot
Strangleroot.publicNotes:
In the shallowest parts of the Darklands, roots sometimes break through cavern ceilings, dangling from above like living stalactites. The most deep-seated of these roots belong to carnivorous trees that draw sustenance not only from the soil, but from the blood of the creatures that wander beneath them. When people on the surface encounter a tree whose leaves are an out-of-season autumnal red, they're likely unaware that, somewhere deep underground, the tree's roots have snared a hapless Darklands creature and are draining its blood.

Darklands inhabitants who live beneath strangleroot forests learn to keep their eyes on the ceiling, where strangleroot taproots lurk. They also watch for desiccated corpses, either strewn about the floor or suspended from the ceiling by hanging roots.

Slow Digestion

Strangleroots might strike with lightning speed, but they have the patience of a slow-growing tree. Once they have a victim trussed up tight, they rarely drain all its blood at once; rather, they do so over the course of hours or days. They accelerate their feeding only to kill a troublesome captive or to engorge themselves, lacing their meal's blood with a poisonous sap as a deterrent against hostile creatures.

While blood engorged, the strangleroot turns red and loses its immunity to bleed damage.

Tajatizt.publicNotes:
To outsiders, the eldritch emeritus looks something like a joke—a befuddled old scholar, their mind so stuffed with obscure theorems and abstract metaphysics that concerns about mere daily reality fade away. Those who know them, however, know that the eldritch emeritus wrote more treatises of spells than most wizards have had hot dinners, and if sufficiently annoyed, is entirely capable of providing a brief, thorough, and fatal demonstration.

True power comes from knowledge—the power to shape the growth of kingdoms by mere whispers, stay three steps ahead of adversaries, or even know which flora is best for creating untraceable poisons.

Thash.publicNotes:
Thashes are elementals that escaped the Plane of Earth millennia ago and now wander the wilds of Sekamina. Resembling ankylosauruses with two tails—one at its back end, and one where its head should be—thashes have no traditional sensory organs. Rather, they experience the world solely through the vibrations they sense in the ground beneath their feet.

Armored in stone and equipped with two smashing tails, thashes are fearless, attacking any creature that wanders into their territory, including other thashes. Since they're inedible, ornery, and not smart enough to have a self-preservation instinct, most Darklands predators avoid them. The only creatures that don't fear thashes are cavern trolls and other rock-eaters, as well as ayindilar elves and the other Darklands cultures who've learned to train them as tireless (if unpredictable) beasts of burden.

Beasts of Burden

Although difficult to train, thashes are both tireless and strong, features that make them excellent beasts of burden for those who know how to control them. Thashes find the vibration of footsteps irresistible. Though a creature that approaches a thash is likely to get their head caved in, a thash will follow anything that keeps a steady pace some distance ahead of them. Difficulty arises only when the time comes to load or unload the thash: cargo and passengers are typically lowered onto the creature's back from above.

action->Involuntary Reaction.description: A creature struck by a raw nerve's nerve ending strike must succeed at a @Check[reflex|dc:34] saving throw or be unable to use reactions until the start of its next turn.

action->Synaptic Overload.name: Synaptic Overload
action->Synaptic Overload.description:
The raw nerve releases a burst of mental energy in a @Template[cone|distance:30], dealing @Damage[6d12[mental]|options:area-damage] damage to each creature in the cone (@Check[will|dc:31|options:area-effect,damaging-effect,inflicts:stunned] save).

Critical Success The creature takes no damage.

Success The creature takes half damage.

Failure The creature takes full damage and is @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.dfCMdR4wnpbYNTix]{Stunned 1}.

Critical Failure The creature takes double damage and is @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.dfCMdR4wnpbYNTix]{Stunned 2}

Thirsty Sands.name: Thirsty Sands
Thirsty Sands.description: Illusory spectators cry out for blood as tendrils of sand hold unwilling combatants in place.
Thirsty Sands.disable: @Check[arcana|dc:38] or @Check[nature|dc:38] (master) twice to undo the magic that animates the sand, @Check[intimidation|dc:34] or @Check[performance|dc:34] (expert) twice to win over the crowd, or @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.spells-srd.Item.9HpwDN4MYQJnW0LG]{Dispel Magic} (9th rank; counteract DC 36)
Thirsty Sands.reset: The hazard deactivates once no living creatures are in the room, resetting after 1 minute.
Thirsty Sands.routine: (1 action) Tendrils of sand rise from the floor. Up to two creatures in the room must attempt a @Check[reflex|dc:38|options:forced-movement,inflicts:prone] save. On a failed save, the tendrils wrap around the creature and move it to an unoccupied square closest to the center of the arena. If the creature was Flying, the tendril also pulls it to the ground. On a critical failure, the creature is also knocked @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.j91X7x0XSomq8d60]{Prone}. The tendrils then collapse back into the floor.

action->The Crowd Goes Wild!.name: The Crowd Goes Wild!
action->The Crowd Goes Wild!.description:
Trigger A living creature enters the area

Effect The chamber fills with the sound of cheering spectators. Each creature in the area attempts a @Check[will|dc:40|options:area-effect,inflicts:confused,inflicts:stunned] saving throw with the effects below. The hazard then rolls initiative.

Critical Success The creature is unaffected.

Success The creature is rattled briefly by the roar and is @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.dfCMdR4wnpbYNTix]{Stunned 1}.

Failure The cries of the bloodthirsty crowd overwhelm the creature. The creature is @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.yblD8fOR1J8rDwEQ]{Confused} for 1 minute but can attempt a new save at the end of each of their turns to end the confusion.

Critical Failure The creature is confused for 1 minute or until the haunt is disabled, with no save to end early.

action->Endless Suffering.name: Endless Suffering
action->Endless Suffering.description:
The type of torture that killed a tormented determines the effect of their Tortured Gaze. The damage type listed in parentheses deactivates their regeneration and is their damage weakness.

Lost in a Maze (mental) The tormented lost themselves in the confusing depths of the Ghostfang Coils. For 1 minute, the target is @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.TBSHQspnbcqxsmjL]{Frightened 1} and @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.e1XGnhKNSQIm5IXg]{Stupefied 1}.

30 feet, or 60 feet if the tormented is at 125 HP or lower.

The psychic agony of a tormented spills into the world around them, creating murderous hallucinations replicating the tormented's last moments. A non-undead creature that ends its turn in the aura must succeed at a @Check[will|dc:32|options:area-effect] save or be @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.TBSHQspnbcqxsmjL]{Frightened 1} and @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.e1XGnhKNSQIm5IXg]{Stupefied 1} for 1 minute. action->Necrotic Decay.name: Necrotic Decay
action->Necrotic Decay.description: When an urdefhan dies, their translucent flesh quickly rots away and sublimates into a foul-smelling gas that fills a @Template[type:emanation|distance:5] around the body. action->Preternatural Parry.name: Preternatural Parry

Trigger Triaza is targeted by a Strike or spell attack roll, or she is about to roll a saving throw against a spell effect

action->Rapid Recharge.name: Rapid Recharge
action->Rapid Recharge.description:

Effect Triaza recharges Bloodthirsty Spellstrike.

action->Wicked Bite.name: Wicked Bite
action->Wicked Bite.description:
Requirements The urdefhan damaged a creature with a jaws Strike on their last action

Effect The urdefhan maintains contact, turning the creature's flesh translucent around the site of the injury. The target must succeed at a @Check[fortitude|dc:36] save or be affected by drain blood or drain vitality (the urdefhan's choice). Vault Lifter.name: Vault Lifter
Vault Lifter.publicNotes:
Vault lifters are sentient stone constructs roughly carved into the semblance of giant xiomorns. Each vault lifter is encircled by a spinning ring, called a rotor, which grants the lifter the ability to fly.

Xiomorns created vault lifters to help construct their vaults throughout the Plane of Earth and across the Universe. With the ability to airlift heavy burdens and possessed with enough intelligence to carry out complex instructions, vault lifters were valuable lieutenants in the xiomorns' vast terraforming projects. Vault lifters were intended to be more than simple laborers, however; they were also built as weapons of war. In combat, vault lifters spin their rotors into fearsome buzz saws capable of propelling them at high speeds and slicing foes in half.

Abandoned Guardians

While some vault lifters continue to serve living xiomorns, others have been left behind in long-abandoned locations. Over the years, many of these forgotten vault lifters have completed their assignments and deactivated themselves. Others continue to perform some unending task, such as "keep this area clean," "prevent unauthorized entry," or "I'll be back in a bit—wait for my return." After millennia spent in solitude, some abandoned vault lifters become fanatical about their final orders, spinning them into complex philosophical systems heavy with moral significance.

action->Activate Rotor.name: Activate Rotor
action->Activate Rotor.description:
The vault lifter's rotor spins, becoming a buzzing blur. While the rotor is activated, the lifter gains a fly Speed of 40 feet. The spinning rotor also creates an aura in a @Template[type:emanation|distance:5] around the lifter. Any creature that enters or starts its turn in the area must attempt a @Check[fortitude|dc:34|options:damaging-effect,forced-movement,inflicts:prone] save.

Critical Success The creature is unaffected, and the vault lifter's rotor is deactivated. The lifter loses its fly Speed and aura until it Activates Rotor again.

Success The creature takes @Damage[2d8[slashing]|options:area-damage] damage.

Failure The creature takes @Damage[4d8[slashing]|options:area-damage] damage.

Critical Failure The creature takes @Damage[8d8[slashing]|options:area-damage] damage. If the creature isn't @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.kWc1fhmv9LBiTuei]{Grabbed} or @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.VcDeM8A5oI6VqhbM]{Restrained} by the vault lifter, they are pushed back 15 feet and knocked @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.j91X7x0XSomq8d60]{Prone}.

action->Carry.name: Carry
action->Carry.description: A vault lifter can Fly at half Speed while it has a creature @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.kWc1fhmv9LBiTuei]{Grabbed} or @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.VcDeM8A5oI6VqhbM]{Restrained}, carrying that creature along with it.

action->Draw In.name: Draw In
action->Draw In.description: The vault lifter attempts to [[/act reposition]] a creature it has @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.kWc1fhmv9LBiTuei]{Grabbed} or @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.VcDeM8A5oI6VqhbM]{Restrained}, moving the creature into a space adjacent to it. This attempt neither applies nor counts toward the lifter's multiple attack penalty.

action->Overdrive.name: Overdrive
action->Overdrive.description:
Requirements The vault lifter's rotor is activated

Effect The lifter Flies up to three times its Fly Speed in a straight line without triggering reactions. At the end of this flight, the lifter must attempt a @Check[fortitude|dc:40] saving throw. On a failure, the lifter's rotor is deactivated.

Vaultquake.name: Vaultquake
Vaultquake.description: The retreating vaultline causes a series of cave-ins.
Vaultquake.disable: @Check[arcana|dc:31], @Check[nature|dc:31], @Check[occultism|dc:31], or @Check[religion|dc:31] (master) to disperse the ley line's power as it retreats, or @Check[survival|dc:27] (expert) to predict where rubble might fall next. The DC of the flat check for this round (see Routine) is increased by 4 on a success or by 8 on a critical success. Increasing the flat check DC to 21 or higher stabilizes the cavern, ending the hazard.
Vaultquake.reset: After 4 rounds, the hazard ends automatically as the vaultquake subsides.
Vaultquake.routine: (1 action) The GM rolls a @Check[flat|dc:9] to determine if a cave-in occurs. On a critical success, the collapse deals @Damage[(2d12+15)[bludgeoning]|options:area-damage] damage to all the PCs instead.

action->Disorienting Screech.name: Disorienting Screech
action->Disorienting Screech.description:

Effect Each creature in the area attempts a @Check[will|dc:30|options:area-effect,inflicts:stunned,inflicts:stupefied] save with the following effects. The hazard then rolls initiative.

Success The creature is unaffected.

Failure The creature is @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.dfCMdR4wnpbYNTix]{Stunned 1} and @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.e1XGnhKNSQIm5IXg]{Stupefied 1} for 1 round.

Critical Failure The creature is @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.dfCMdR4wnpbYNTix]{Stunned 2} and stupefied 1 for an indefinite duration.

Vemerak.name: Vemerak
Vemerak.publicNotes:
A vemerak looks like a mishmash between a burrowing insect and a grotesque sea creature, stretched and warped to a titanic scale. When it first bursts from a half-buried hidey-hole or scuttles down a narrow tunnel, its form is obscured by a tangle of spidery legs and tentacles. Only when an unfortunate witness views the creature up close is the vemerak's immense, ant-like body revealed. At one end of the beast, glittering eyes blink above short, wriggling tentacles and serrated mouthparts, while three tail-like tentacles wave and slap at the other. Blue-green mold flakes from the vemerak's flanks, and wherever the mold lands, magic around it fades.

With its clicking pincers and corrosive bile, the vemerak is often mistaken for a mindless predator like a scorpion or spider, but it has enough wit to speak to its intended prey. A vemerak's words are often cruel, focused on the pain it plans to inflict on its victims.

Though most often encountered in the Darklands, in ages past vemeraks roamed Golarion's surface, leaving chaos and suffering in their wake. The creatures have even been encountered on other planets in Golarion's solar system, such as the distant Triaxus.

Rovagug's Pets

Though in its natural state a vemerak is hardly more intelligent than a predatory animal, its mind is linked to the urges and drives of the god Rovagug. When slaughter is in the offing, a vemerak becomes capable of laying traps with cunning and foresight, and its otherwise limited vocabulary grows poetic as it threatens foes with suffering and death. The farther a vemerak travels from Golarion's depths, the more tenuous its link to Rovagug becomes. Vemeraks found in the shallower parts of the Darklands are as mindless as cave worms or giant insects.

action->Dispelling Spores.name: Dispelling Spores
action->Dispelling Spores.description: 30 feet. The vemerak's body exudes antimagic spores. When an ongoing spell effect enters the aura, the vemerak automatically attempts to counteract it ([[/r 1d20+28 #Counteract]]{+28} counteract modifier, 7th rank). The spell effect is then temporarily immune to the vemerak's dispelling spores for 24 hours.

action->Bile Spray.name: Bile Spray
action->Bile Spray.description: The vemerak breathes a blast of pale blue corrosive bile that deals @Damage[14d6[acid]|options:area-damage] damage in a @Template[type:line|distance:90] (@Check[reflex|dc:34|basic|options:area-effect,inflicts:sickened] save). A creature that fails its save is also @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.fesd1n5eVhpCSS18]{Sickened 1} (@UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.fesd1n5eVhpCSS18]{Sickened 2} on a critical failure). The vemerak can't use Bile Spray again for [[/gmr 1d4 #Recharge Bile Spray]]{1d4 rounds}.

action->Earthquake.name: Earthquake
action->Earthquake.description: The vemerak digs its tentacles into the earth or stone beneath it. At the start of the vemerak's next turn, if the vemerak hasn't been moved or knocked @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.j91X7x0XSomq8d60]{Prone} and is able to take actions, it creates the effects of an @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.spells-srd.Item.x7SPrsRxGb2Vy2nu]{Earthquake} spell, centered on the vemerak, without using an action to do so. The vemerak ignores difficult terrain and the penalty to attack rolls, AC, and skill checks created by shaking ground, and it can exclude itself from any other effects created by the earthquake.

action->Eyespots.name: Eyespots
action->Eyespots.description: A warpigrade can't see anything beyond 30 feet.

action->Tun State.name: Tun State
action->Tun State.description:
Trigger The warpigrade would be reduced to 0 Hit Points or would die due to starvation, suffocation, or similar environmental causes

Frequency once per week

Requirements The warpigrade isn't already in tun state

Effect The warpigrade doesn't die but instead remains at 1 Hit Point and curls into a dry ball, called a tun. While in this tun state, the warpigrade is @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.fBnFDH2MTzgFijKf]{Unconscious}, doesn't need to eat, drink, or breathe, and doubles its resistance to 20. It remains in tun state indefinitely until covered in significant amounts of water, at which point it begins to rehydrate, gaining regeneration 5. The regeneration persists until it reaches maximum Hit Points. The warpigrade then exits its tun state.

action->Ingest Aspect.description:

Effect The warpigrade makes a stylet Strike. If it succeeds, the warpigrade attempts to absorb some of the victim's essence. The creature attempts a @Check[fortitude|dc:33] save.

Success The creature becomes @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.i3OJZU2nk64Df3xm]{Clumsy 1} or @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.MIRkyAjyBeXivMa7]{Enfeebled 1} (determine randomly) for 1 round. If the creature becomes clumsy, the warpigrade gains a +1 status bonus to its AC and Reflex save for 1 round; if the creature becomes enfeebled, the warpigrade instead gains the bonus to its attack and damage rolls.

Failure As success, except if the creature is already clumsy or enfeebled, the condition value and corresponding status bonus increase by 1 (to a maximum of 4), and the effect lasts for 1 minute.

Critical Failure As failure, except the condition value and status bonus increase by 2.

action->Vacuum Mouth.name: Vacuum Mouth
action->Vacuum Mouth.description:
Requirements The warpigrade doesn't have a target @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.kWc1fhmv9LBiTuei]{Grabbed}

Effect The warpigrade draws in air with its mouth. All creatures in a @Template[cone|distance:20] must succeed at a @Check[reflex|dc:30|options:area-effect,forced-movement] save or be pulled adjacent to the warpigrade. The warpigrade chooses one creature that failed its save, Grabbing the target in its claws and making a stylet Strike.

Wet Blanket.name: Wet Blanket
Wet Blanket.description: Wet Blanket's invisible spirit plays a discordant tune that confounds the senses.
Wet Blanket.disable: @Check[diplomacy|dc:40] or @Check[intimidation|dc:40] (expert) twice to convince Wet Blanket to stay silent, @Check[occultism|dc:42] or @Check[religion|dc:42] (master) to exorcise Wet Blanket's spirit, or @Check[performance|dc:38] (expert) twice to drown out Wet Blanket's music. A PC holding Wet Blanket's fiddle of the maestro gains a +2 item bonus to any check made to disable the haunt.
Wet Blanket.reset: Unless the haunt is disabled, Wet Blanket falls silent once all creatures leave the room. She returns if another creature moves adjacent to the gate.
Wet Blanket.routine:
(1 action; auditory, concentrate, emotion, incapacitation, mental) Wet Blanket's tune causes creatures who hear it to act irrationally. Yig.languages: speak with animals (reptiles only), telepathy 100 feet
Yig.publicNotes:
To call Yig benign is perhaps too generous, but among the eldritch entities that comprise the Great Old Ones and Outer Gods, the word is indeed apropos. While those who worship Yig know that the patience of the so-called Father of Serpents is limited and expect no kindness from him, Yig nonetheless seeks vengeance against those who harm his beloved serpents—and sometimes his non-serpent worshippers as well.

Great Old Ones

Although Yig is one of the least powerful of the Great Old Ones, his might vastly outstrips that of most mortal creatures. He exists outside of the cycle of souls and is immortal—if a way exists that Yig can be permanently slain, none yet know it. Likewise, no one can say for certain where Yig's home world lies. Indeed, the Great Old One counts any world on which serpents might be found as his own.

Yig's Worshippers

Yig has worshippers on many worlds, and unlike most Great Old Ones, he sometimes takes notice of those who venerate him. He has even been known to reward his faithful from time to time—a trait not shared by the other Great Old Ones. Worship of Yig has long been a point of friction in sekmin society, where venerating deities other than Ydersius is often synonymous with treason. Additional information concerning Yig's worshippers, including his clerics, appears on pages 318–319 of Pathfinder Lost Omens Divine Mysteries.

spell->Rune Trap.description:
You create a magical trap by binding a hostile spell into a rune. As part of performing this ritual, you also Cast a Spell to store in the rune. The stored spell must take 3 actions or fewer to cast, have a hostile effect, and target one creature or have an area. You can set a password, a trigger, or both for the rune. Any creature that moves, opens, or touches the target container or enters the target area that doesn't speak the password or that matches the trigger activates the rune, releasing the harmful spell within.

Once a spell is stored in the rune, the rune gains all the traits of that spell. If the stored spell targets one or more creatures, it targets the creature that set off the rune. If it has an area, that area is centered on the creature that set off the rune. The rune is a magical trap, using your spell DC for both the Perception check to notice it and the Thievery check to disable it; both checks require the creature attempting them to be trained in order to succeed. You can Dismiss the rune you create with this ritual so long as you can see it.

Success You create the rune successfully.

Failure You fail to create the rune.

Zyss Assassin.name: Zyss Assassin
Zyss Assassin.publicNotes:
Potential zyss assassins are selected from among the offspring of high-ranking sekmins and trained to remove threats both external and internal. In sekmin culture, to die at the hand of a zyss assassin is considered an honorable fate (though not one that's generally desired). Despite this elite status, the training zyss assassins must undergo is both rigorous and cruel. Zyss assassins train for years, learning to rely on no weapon other than those with which they were born, and submit to painful procedures to gain their most fearsome tool: their extraordinarily corrosive spit.

Although zyss assassins are perfectly happy to work alone, they're often deployed in groups of three or more. While one assailant wraps a target in their coils, their confederates strike with poisoned fangs. If their attack is successful, the target's corpse is dissolved with acid, leaving no trace behind.

Serpentfolk society is riddled with secret organizations, many of which preserve long-lost traditions from the height of the ancient sekmin empire. Exclusive orders of aapoph sovereign guards and zyss assassins, among others, trace their origins back millennia, training in the same techniques they employed in the days when mammalian humanoids were nothing but servants or prey.

Leave no Trace

Over the course of centuries, zyss assassins have carried out assignments for nearly every faction within sekmin culture. The common thread of these missions is that they each required plausible deniability. To that end, every zyss assassin is implanted with acid sacs harvested from a vemerak's stomach. Not only can a zyss use their corrosive spit to dissolve their victims, but when a zyss assassin dies, their body explodes in a burst of acidic sludge that leaves behind no evidence of their existence.
